items.prompt: Tap every square the white bishop on c4 attacks (a square with a piece on it counts if the bishop attacks that piece).

claims.statement: The bishop on c4 attacks exactly these squares.

hints: A bishop moves on diagonals; there are four directions from c4.
In each direction include squares until you meet a piece, and include that square too.
One direction ends on f7, the Black pawn.
items.explain: The bishop sees a2, b3, d3, e2, f1, b5, a6, d5, e6 and stops at f7, the first piece on that diagonal.

items.prompt: One change: Black's e-pawn went to e6, not e5. Tap every square the white bishop on c4 attacks now.

claims.statement: The bishop on c4 attacks exactly these squares.

hints: Follow the same diagonals as before.
The long diagonal toward Black's king side now meets a pawn earlier.
It stops at e6; f7 is no longer on the list.
items.explain: The pawn on e6 is the first piece on the diagonal, so the bishop reaches e6 and no further: f7 is not attacked.

items.prompt: White to move. Compared with the moment after the bishop arrived on c4, is f7 now an easier or a harder target?

claims.statement: One white piece attacks f7.
Two black pieces defend f7.

hints: Count the attackers of f7, then count the defenders.
The king is not alone any more.
One attacker against two defenders.
items.explain: One attacker (the bishop) now faces two defenders (king and rook), so the pressure has no chance to win the pawn.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the bishop move that develops the bishop and attacks f7, a pawn guarded only by its king.

claims.statement: Black's king is the only defender of f7.
The move is legal.
After the bishop goes to c4 it attacks f7.

hints: Which White piece has a diagonal toward f7 once it leaves f1?
The bishop needs a square on the a2 to g8 diagonal.
Bishop to c4.
items.explain: From c4 the bishop looks along the diagonal to f7. After the move one white piece attacks f7, and only the king defends it.

feedback_by_move.f1b5: The bishop on b5 attacks the knight on c6, not f7.
feedback_by_move.f1e2: The bishop on e2 develops but attacks nothing in Black's camp.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the pawn move that prepares the central break d4 by giving that break a pawn recapture.

claims.statement: The pawn on c3 would attack d4.
c3 and d3 are both sound: the engine's best move is one of them and both are within 40 centipawns.

hints: Which pawn could end up attacking d4?
A pawn on the third rank can recapture on the fourth.
The c-pawn steps to c3.
items.explain: From c3 the pawn attacks d4, so after d4 exd4 White can retake with the c-pawn. Both c3 and d3 are sound; they aim at different structures.

feedback_by_move.d2d3: d3 is sound but it closes the centre; it does not prepare the d4 break.

items.prompt: White's bishop is on c4. Which Black piece or pawn does it attack?

claims.statement: One white piece attacks f7.
No white piece attacks c6.

hints: Look along the diagonal from c4.
The diagonal runs c4, d5, e6, f7.
The pawn on f7.
items.explain: The diagonal from c4 meets the pawn on f7 first.

items.prompt: White's bishop is on b5 instead. Which Black piece or pawn does it attack?

claims.statement: No white piece attacks f7.
One white piece attacks c6.

hints: Look along the diagonal from b5.
The first piece it meets is Black's.
The knight on c6.
items.explain: From b5 the diagonal toward Black's side meets the knight on c6; f7 is out of reach.

items.prompt: White's bishop is on e2 instead. Which Black piece or pawn does it attack?

claims.statement: The bishop on e2 attacks exactly these squares, none holding a Black piece.

hints: Check every diagonal from e2.
The diagonals meet your own pieces or empty squares.
None of them: no Black piece is attacked.
items.explain: The bishop on e2 sees only empty squares and its own pieces, so it attacks nothing in Black's camp.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find Black's best reply.

claims.statement: The engine's best move is Qxg5 and it is far ahead of the alternatives.
The knight on g5 is attacked and undefended.
After Qxg5 the engine rates Black at least three pawns better.

hints: Is every white piece protected?
Look at the knight on g5 and count who attacks it and who defends it.
The queen on d8 sees g5 along an open diagonal.
items.explain: The knight on g5 has no defender and the queen on d8 attacks it down an open diagonal. Counting only the target squares misses the loose attacker.

feedback_by_move.d7d5: Hitting the bishop is not enough: the loose knight on g5 can simply be taken.
feedback_by_move.g8h6: Guarding f7 passively gives up the chance to win the knight.

items.prompt: White to move. White attacks f7 twice and only the king defends it. Is it a good moment to capture on f7?

claims.statement: Two white pieces attack f7.
One black piece defends f7.
A capture on f7 is the engine's choice (Nxf7 and Bxf7+ both within 40 centipawns of the best).
The engine rates the position at least six-tenths of a pawn better for White (depth 16).

hints: Count attackers and defenders of f7, then ask whether Black has a defender on the way.
The queen's diagonal is blocked by the knight on f6.
Yes: nothing else guards f7 and no counterattack is faster.
items.explain: Two attackers against one defender, no other Black piece can reach f7 in time, and the engine at depth 16 prefers capturing. This is the Traxler Counterattack in our opening data.

items.prompt: Black to move. Which developing reply attacks the pawn on e4?

claims.statement: The engine's best move is Nf6, which attacks the loose pawn on e4.
The engine rates the position between level and about a third of a pawn for White.
h6 is rated at least 20 centipawns lower than the best reply.
Nh6 is rated at least 50 centipawns lower than the best reply.
After Nf6 the pawn on e4 is attacked and undefended.

hints: Which Black piece can reach a square from which it attacks e4?
The pawn on e4 has no defender yet.
Knight to f6.
items.explain: Nf6 develops and attacks e4 at once. Bc5 is also sound and develops, but it aims at f2, not at e4. The engine rates h6 and Nh6 lower at depth 16: neither develops, and neither is needed yet.

feedback_by_move.h7h6: h6 stops a knight jump to g5 but develops nothing; the engine at depth 16 rates it lower than the developing replies, though the gap is small.
feedback_by_move.g8h6: The knight on the rim guards f7 but is passive; the engine rates this clearly lower (depth 16).
feedback_by_move.f8e7: Safe and slow, and it does not attack e4: the engine gives White a bigger edge than after Nf6 or Bc5.
feedback_by_move.d7d6: A solid move, rated lower than the developing replies at depth 16.
feedback_by_move.f8c5: Bc5 is a sound developing move, but it attacks f2, not e4.

claims.statement: The bishop on c4 attacks exactly these squares (f7 holds a pawn; c6, e5 and d5 are not attacked pieces).
No white piece attacks c6.

hints: Follow the diagonals from c4 and note where each ends.
The diagonal toward Black's king side ends on a black pawn.
The pawn on f7.
items.explain: The diagonal from c4 meets the pawn on f7 first. The bishop does not attack the knight on c6 or the pawn on e5, and d5 is an empty square.

items.prompt: Black to move. White has played the knight to g5. Find Black's best reply.

claims.statement: The engine's best move is Nh6 or Qf6; both within 40 centipawns.
Qxg5 is rated at least six pawns worse than Nh6.

hints: Is the knight on g5 protected this time?
The bishop on c1 sees g5 through the empty d2 square.
Add a second guard for f7.
items.explain: The bishop on c1 defends g5, so the queen takes nothing. The knight on h6 adds a second guard for f7; the queen on f6 also guards f7 and hits the knight, and the engine rates it a little lower than Nh6.

feedback_by_move.d8g5: The knight is defended by the bishop on c1, so Qxg5 loses the queen for a knight.

items.prompt: Black to move. Is Black bound to lose the pawn on f7?

claims.statement: Two white pieces attack f7.
One black piece defends f7.
White has no advantage here: the engine rates the position level or better for Black (depth 16).

hints: Count the pieces that can still arrive to guard f7.
Black has not castled yet.
Castling brings the rook to f8.
items.explain: Black can castle, adding the rook as a second defender; the engine rates the position level or slightly better for Black.

items.prompt: White to move. Which move develops a minor piece?

claims.statement: The bishop on f1 blocks castling.
The bishop move to c4 is legal.
After the bishop goes to c4 it attacks f7.

hints: Which of these moves brings a knight or a bishop into play?
The queen move develops a queen, not a minor piece.
The bishop travels on the long diagonal.
items.explain: Only the bishop move develops a minor piece; the bishop on f1 was also blocking castling, and from c4 it attacks f7.

items.prompt: White to move. Can White castle right now?

claims.statement: Castling kingside is legal.

hints: Which squares lie between the king and the rook?
Both f1 and g1 are empty.
Yes: castling is already possible.
items.explain: The bishop and the knight have left f1 and g1, so castling is already legal after only three moves.
